extracted.intended_audience: academic economists, political-economy and education policy researchers, and graduate students
extracted.subtask_description: Empirical evaluation of a large historical public-education expansion (Indonesia's SD INPRES) using administrative and survey data with multiple identification strategies to study school entry, school choice, and ideological impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of novel, granular administrative and survey data
rubrics_metrics.description: Combine newly compiled administrative registries (MORA madrasa and pesantren, MEC/Dapodik secular schools) with nationally-representative surveys (Susenas, IFLS), village censuses (Podes), SIAP curriculum timetables, electoral data, and the 2010 Population Census.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper emphasizes complete coverage of school registries (dates, village/district, grade level), linking across sources, and leveraging establishment-year information to identify entry responses. It uses multiple data sources to cross-check and mitigate survivorship/attrition bias (e.g., Podes). Anti-pattern: relying on a single incomplete registry or uncoded curriculum strings without validation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear outcome taxonomy: school entry, school choice, ideological impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Focus analysis on three types of outcomes: (i) Islamic school entry, (ii) school choice along secular–religious dimension, and (iii) downstream ideological/identity effects among cohorts and their children.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure empirical work so that mechanisms and identification strategies map to each outcome separately. Provide descriptive and causal evidence for each outcome class rather than collapsing them.

rubrics_metrics.name: District-level difference-in-differences identification with fixed effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimate balanced panel at the district-year level y_jt = θ_j + θ_t + β INPRES_jt + (X'_j θ_t)' η + ε_jt, where y is Islamic school entries per 1,000 children, and control for district and year fixed effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Control flexibly for time-varying trends by interacting year fixed effects with INPRES targeting variables. Cluster standard errors at the district level. Anti-pattern: running simple DID without accounting for targeting or district heterogeneity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for INPRES targeting variables and differential trends
rubrics_metrics.description: Control for the policy's allocation determinants (1971 child population, enrollment rates, concurrent programs) and interact these with year fixed effects, and separately interact year FE with pre-existing prevalence of Islamic schools in 1959.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures estimates are conditional on initial enrollment and population levels and mitigates confounding from the program's non-random allocation. Anti-pattern: ignoring the program rule that allocated more schools to areas with more non-enrolled children.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of synthetic difference-in-differences (SDID) for robustness to parallel-trends violations
rubrics_metrics.description: Implement Arkhangelsky et al. (2021) SDID by discretizing INPRES exposure (e.g., above 51st percentile) to reweight and match pre-INPRES trends across high- and low-exposure districts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SDID provides more robust comparisons when parallel trends may not hold; it trades-off some variation for better pre-trend balance. Use SDID alongside standard DID as complementary evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Village-level exploitation of staggered treatment timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Exploit the staggered entry of SD INPRES at the village level to obtain more granular identification of entry effects, particularly at the primary (elementary) level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Staggered-treatment designs can help validate district-level results and give a clearer view of timing. Use event-study visuals at the village level to check dynamics. Anti-pattern: relying only on cross-sectional variation without leveraging timing heterogeneity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Event-study visualizations and checking pre-trends
rubrics_metrics.description: Plot semi-decade and annual event-study estimates allowing β to vary over time to visualize dynamic responses and to inspect for pre-trends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present event-study graphs for both DID and SDID specifications to show the timing of effects and pre-treatment parallelism. Use formal tests (e.g., Roth and Rambachan) to assess pre-trends as robustness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Robustness to survivorship/attrition bias in registries
rubrics_metrics.description: Address potential survivor bias in 2019 registries by validating entry increases in historical administrative data (Podes 1980–1993) and showing missing establishment years are uncorrelated with INPRES intensity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Triangulate with independent historical sources and document missingness patterns. Anti-pattern: assuming modern registries reflect historical entry without validation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and measurement of treatment intensity
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure INPRES exposure as number of SD INPRES schools per 1,000 children (1971 baseline), and for SDID set binary indicator for districts above the 51st percentile in INPRES construction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly define treatment scales and justify discretization choices when required by methods. Sensitivity checks to alternative normalization should be reported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clustering and inference choices
rubrics_metrics.description: Cluster standard errors at the district level for district-year panel regressions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match clustering level to the unit of treatment variation. Report how inference is handled under staggered adoption and SDID; consider robustness to alternative clustering and small-sample adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coding and measurement of curriculum content
rubrics_metrics.description: Parse SIAP weekly timetable strings for each school-grade and code each course into categories (Islamic subjects, Pancasila/civic, Bahasa Indonesia, Arabic, math, natural sciences, humanities, thematic) using regular expressions and manually coded title lists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concrete keyword lists and regex rules (examples: 'PPKn' for Pancasila, 'Arab' for Arabic, 'Matematika' for math). Link SIAP records to MORA registry via school IDs. Note selective reporting (SIAP covers ~20% of madrasa) and discuss potential selection biases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational definition of 'Islamic schooling' in surveys
rubrics_metrics.description: Define Islamic schooling in Susenas as the union of (a) final level of schooling certified and (b) final level attended; results robust to restricting to either component.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about how mixed attendance/completion is classified (e.g., secular primary + some Islamic junior secondary). Conduct sensitivity checks to alternative definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mechanism tests via resource mobilization (waqf and informal taxation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Test whether Islamic sector entry response was stronger in villages with larger pre-existing waqf base and greater exposure to a concurrent rice price shock, linking entry to available revenue streams (waqf, infaq, zakat).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure local capacity to finance school construction and interact with INPRES intensity to test the mobilization mechanism. Use qualitative evidence (oral histories) to corroborate quantitative heterogeneity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examine formalization and substitution among school types
rubrics_metrics.description: Document that formal madrasa entry rose while informal diniyah/pesantren behavior changed (informal institutions decreased as a fraction of new Islamic schools), indicating formalization induced by competition with the state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare entry patterns across school types and levels; report shares and substitution patterns. Anti-pattern: treating all private/religious schools as homogeneous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heterogeneity analysis by gender and ideology
rubrics_metrics.description: Explore differences in school choice and treatment effects across subgroups (e.g., female students, cohorts exposed to veil ban, regions with historical Islamic party support).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-specify subgroup analyses motivated by institutional context (e.g., veil ban) and political history (vote shares). Interpret heterogeneous effects in light of plausible mechanisms (preferences, constraints).

rubrics_metrics.name: Linking schooling changes to downstream identity and intergenerational outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure outcomes such as Arabic literacy, religiosity indices, support for Pancasila, and language use at home; test whether cohort exposure to SD INPRES affected these and whether effects transmit to next generation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use census and survey proxies (Arabic literacy, primary home language) and intergenerational linkages in survey data to assess persistence. Conduct robustness checks for composition and migration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modeling framework to interpret empirical patterns
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a Hotelling-style model of competition where students differ in religious preferences and schools choose markets and curriculum emphasis to derive predictions on entry and differentiation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complement empirical findings with a simple theoretical model to generate testable predictions (e.g., when competition leads to more religious differentiation). Provide formal derivations in appendices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control for concurrent confounders and political events
rubrics_metrics.description: Account for other contemporaneous policies/events (Transmigration, Village Law 1979, suppression of separatist movements, Decrees on curriculum and uniforms) that may confound estimates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include controls or robustness checks for these events; discuss pathways through which they could bias estimates. Use historical narrative and qualitative evidence to contextualize identification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detailed data construction and matching transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Document village-level fuzzy merges across registries using province/district/subdistrict/village with a high threshold (0.95), and report match rates (e.g., 80% for Dapodik, 84% for MORA madrasa).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe matching algorithms, thresholds, and success rates; make code/keyword lists and data dictionaries available where possible. Anti-pattern: failing to document matching steps or match quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide online appendix and reproducibility materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Make an online appendix and data appendix available (URL provided) with additional tables, figures, and methodological details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure transparency by releasing appendices, robustness tables, coding lists (e.g., course title mappings), and description of omitted observations. If data confidentiality limits sharing, provide code and simulated examples.
